document_summary: AAGLA industry article (posted May 16, 2025) explaining the City of Los Angeles requirement that landlords of rent-stabilized (LARSO) units pay tenants interest on security deposits under LAMC 151.06.02, with a table of annual interest rates.

rules.title: Security deposit interest for RSO units (LAMC 151.06.02)
rules.requirement: Landlords of rent-stabilized units must pay tenants accrued interest on security deposits, either as a direct payment or a rent credit, on a monthly or yearly basis, and must tell the tenant in writing which method they chose. The City sets the interest rate annually.
rules.key_value: Interest paid monthly or yearly at the City-set annual rate (4.320% for calendar year 2025)
rules.coverage_conditions: Properties within the City of Los Angeles subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (LARSO).
rules.interaction: Applies in addition to state security deposit law (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5); this document does not discuss that interaction.
rules.quoted_span: A tenant shall be given the unpaid accrued interest in the form of either a direct payment or a credit against the tenant’s rent. The landlord shall choose between these two methods of payment and notify the tenant in writing of his or her choice. The landlord may elect to pay the accrued interest on a monthly or yearly basis.
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary source (landlord association article) quoting the LAMC. The quoted text says interest 'shall begin accruing on November 1, 1990', which is an accrual date and not a stated effective date, so effective_date is null. The rate table runs through 2025 only (4.320%, updated 5/21/25); rates for 2026 are not in this capture. Article notes laws may have changed since publication.
